s: oṃ devā ha vai svargalokam āyaṃs te rudram apṛcchan ko bhavān iti | so 'bravīd aham ekaḥ prathamam āsodvartāmi ca bhaviṣyāmi ca nānyaḥ kaścin matto vyatirikta iti | so 'ntarād antaraṃ prāviśat diśaś cāntaraṃ prāviśat so 'haṃ nityānityo vyaktāvyakto brahmā brahmāhaṃ prāñcaḥ pratyañco 'haṃ dakṣiṇāṃ ca udañco 'ham adhaś cordhvaś cāhaṃ diśaś ca pratidiśaś cāhaṃ pumān apumān striyaś cāhaṃ sāvitry ahaṃ gāyatry ahaṃ triṣṭubjagatyanuṣṭup cāhaṃ chando 'haṃ satyo 'haṃ gārhapatyo dakṣiṇāgnir āhavanīyo 'haṃ gaur ahaṃ gaury aham ṛg ahaṃ yajur ahaṃ sāmāham atharvāṅgiraso 'haṃ jyeṣṭho 'haṃ śreṣṭho'haṃ variṣṭho 'ham āpo 'haṃ tejo 'haṃ guhyo 'ham araṇyo 'ham akṣaram ahaṃ kṣaram ahaṃ puṣkaram ahaṃ pavitram aham ugraṃ ca baliś ca purastāj jyotir ity aham eva sarvebhyo mām eva sa sarvaḥ samāyo māṃ veda sa devān veda sarvāṃś ca vedān sāṅgān api brahma brāhmaṇaiś ca gāṃ gobhir brāhmaṇān brāhmaṇyena havir haviṣā āyur āyuṣā satyena satyaṃ dharmeṇa dharmaṃ tarpayāmi svena tejasā | tato ha vai te devā rudram apṛcchan te devā rudram apaśyan te devā rudram adhyāyan te devā ūrdhvabāhavo rudraṃ stuvanti ||
d: ओं देवा ह वै स्वर्गलोकम् आयंस् ते रुद्रम् अपृच्छन् को भवान् इति । सो ऽब्रवीद् अहम् एकः प्रथमम् आसोद्वर्तामि च भविष्यामि च नान्यः कश्चिन् मत्तो व्यतिरिक्त इति । सो ऽन्तराद् अन्तरं प्राविशत् दिशश् चान्तरं प्राविशत् सो ऽहं नित्यानित्यो व्यक्ताव्यक्तो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्माहं प्राञ्चः प्रत्यञ्चो ऽहं दक्षिणां च उदञ्चो ऽहम् अधश् चोर्ध्वश् चाहं दिशश् च प्रतिदिशश् चाहं पुमान् अपुमान् स्त्रियश् चाहं सावित्र्य् अहं गायत्र्य् अहं त्रिष्टुब्जगत्यनुष्टुप् चाहं छन्दो ऽहं सत्यो ऽहं गार्हपत्यो दक्षिणाग्निर् आहवनीयो ऽहं गौर् अहं गौर्य् अहम् ऋग् अहं यजुर् अहं सामाहम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसो ऽहं ज्येष्ठो ऽहं श्रेष्ठोऽहं वरिष्ठो ऽहम् आपो ऽहं तेजो ऽहं गुह्यो ऽहम् अरण्यो ऽहम् अक्षरम् अहं क्षरम् अहं पुष्करम् अहं पवित्रम् अहम् उग्रं च बलिश् च पुरस्ताज् ज्योतिर् इत्य् अहम् एव सर्वेभ्यो माम् एव स सर्वः समायो मां वेद स देवान् वेद सर्वांश् च वेदान् साङ्गान् अपि ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणैश् च गां गोभिर् ब्राह्मणान् ब्राह्मण्येन हविर् हविषा आयुर् आयुषा सत्येन सत्यं धर्मेण धर्मं तर्पयामि स्वेन तेजसा । ततो ह वै ते देवा रुद्रम् अपृच्छन् ते देवा रुद्रम् अपश्यन् ते देवा रुद्रम् अध्यायन् ते देवा ऊर्ध्वबाहवो रुद्रं स्तुवन्ति ॥
m:
Om. The gods, indeed, went to the heavenly world; they asked Rudra: "Who are you?"
He said: "I alone was at first, I am, and I shall be; no other whatsoever exists apart from me."
He entered the inner from the inner; he entered the cardinal directions and the interior. "I am the eternal and the non-eternal, the manifest and the unmanifest, Brahman and non-Brahman. I am the eastern and the western, the southern and the northern. I am below and above, the cardinal directions and the intermediate directions. I am male, neuter, and female. I am the Sāvitrī meter, the Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh meter, the Jagatī meter, and the Anuṣṭubh meter. I am the meter, I am truth, I am the Gārhapatya fire, the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, and the Āhavanīya fire. I am the bull, I am the cow. I am the Ṛg, I am the Yajus, I am the Sāman, I am the Atharvāṅgiras. I am the eldest, I am the best, I am the foremost. I am the waters, I am splendor, I am the secret, I am the forest. I am the imperishable, I am the perishable, I am the lotus, I am the purifier. [I am] the fierce and the offering, the light in the east—thus am I alone of all things. Whoever knows me as all this, he knows all; he knows the gods, and all the Vedas together with their limbs; and [he knows] Brahman through the brahmins. I satisfy the cow with cows, the brahmins with brahminhood, the oblation with the oblation, life with life, truth with truth, righteousness with righteousness, by my own splendor."
Then, indeed, those gods asked Rudra; those gods saw Rudra; those gods meditated upon Rudra; those gods, raising their arms upward, praise Rudra:

s: oṃ yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yaś ca brahmā tasmai vai namonamaḥ ||
d: ओं यो वै रुद्रः स भगवान् यश् च ब्रह्मा तस्मै वै नमोनमः ॥

He who is Rudra is the Blessed One, and what is the earth—to him, indeed, reverence, reverence!

s: bhas te ādir madhyaṃ bhuvas te svas te śīrṣaṃ viśvarūpo 'si brahmaikas tvaṃ dvidhā tridhā vṛddhis tvaṃ śāntis tvaṃ puṣṭis tvaṃ hutam ahutaṃ dattam adattaṃ sarvam asarvaṃ viśvam aviśvaṃ kṛtam akṛtaṃ param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ca tvam | apām asomam amṛtā abhūm āgan me jyotir avidāma devān | kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ | kim u dhūrtir amṛtaṃ martyasya somasūryapurastāt sūkṣmaḥ puruṣaḥ | sarvaṃ jagaddhitaṃ vā etad akṣaraṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ puruṣaṃ grāhyam aguhyena bhāvaṃ bhāvena saumyaṃ saumyena sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmena vāyavyaṃ vāyavyena grasati tasmai mahāgrāsāya vai namonamaḥ | hṛdisthā devatāḥ sarvā hṛdi prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ | hṛdi tvam asi yo nityaṃ tisro mātrāḥ paras tu saḥ ||
d: भस् ते आदिर् मध्यं भुवस् ते स्वस् ते शीर्षं विश्वरूपो ऽसि ब्रह्मैकस् त्वं द्विधा त्रिधा वृद्धिस् त्वं शान्तिस् त्वं पुष्टिस् त्वं हुतम् अहुतं दत्तम् अदत्तं सर्वम् असर्वं विश्वम् अविश्वं कृतम् अकृतं परम् अपरं परायणं च त्वम् । अपाम् असोमम् अमृता अभूम् आगन् मे ज्योतिर् अविदाम देवान् । किं नूनम् अस्मान् कृणवद् अरातिः । किम् उ धूर्तिर् अमृतं मर्त्यस्य सोमसूर्यपुरस्तात् सूक्ष्मः पुरुषः । सर्वं जगद्धितं वा एतद् अक्षरं प्राजापत्यं सौम्यं सूक्ष्मं पुरुषं ग्राह्यम् अगुह्येन भावं भावेन सौम्यं सौम्येन सूक्ष्मं सूक्ष्मेन वायव्यं वायव्येन ग्रसति तस्मै महाग्रासाय वै नमोनमः । हृदिस्था देवताः सर्वा हृदि प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । हृदि त्वम् असि यो नित्यं तिस्रो मात्राः परस् तु सः ॥
m:
Bhūḥ is your beginning; Bhuvaḥ is your middle; Svaḥ is your head. You are omniform, the one Brahman, twofold, threefold. You are growth, you are peace, you are prosperity; the offered and the unoffered, the given and the ungiven, the all and the not-all, the whole and the not-whole, the done and the undone, the higher, the lower, and the supreme goal are you.
We have drunk Soma, we have become immortal; we have reached the light, we have found the gods.
What now can malice do to us?
What indeed the deceit, O immortal one, of a mortal? In front of Soma and Sūrya is the subtle Puruṣa.
Beneficial to the whole world indeed is this imperishable, born of Prajāpati, gentle, subtle Puruṣa, to be grasped by what is not hidden: he swallows existence by existence, the gentle by the gentle, the subtle by the subtle, the aerial by the aerial. To him, indeed, the great swallower, reverence, reverence!
All the deities are established in the heart; the vital breaths are established in the heart;
In the heart are you who are eternal; but that one who is beyond the three moras is he.

s: tasyottarataḥ śirodakṣiṇataḥ pādau ya uttarataḥ sa oṃkāraḥ ya oṃkāraḥ sa praṇavaḥ yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa sarvavyāpī yaḥ sarvavyāpī so 'nantaḥ yo 'nantas tat tāraṃ yat tāraṃ tac chuklaṃ yac chuklaṃ tat sūkṣmaṃ yat sūkṣmaṃ tad vaidyutaṃ yad vaidyutaṃ tat paraṃ brahma yat paraṃ brahma sa ekaḥ yaḥ ekaḥ sa rudraḥ yo rudraḥ sa īśānaḥ ya īśānaḥ sa bhagavān maheśvaraḥ ||
d: तस्योत्तरतः शिरोदक्षिणतः पादौ य उत्तरतः स ओंकारः य ओंकारः स प्रणवः यः प्रणवः स सर्वव्यापी यः सर्वव्यापी सो ऽनन्तः यो ऽनन्तस् तत् तारं यत् तारं तच् छुक्लं यच् छुक्लं तत् सूक्ष्मं यत् सूक्ष्मं तद् वैद्युतं यद् वैद्युतं तत् परं ब्रह्म यत् परं ब्रह्म स एकः यः एकः स रुद्रः यो रुद्रः स ईशानः य ईशानः स भगवान् महेश्वरः ॥
m: His head is to the north, his two feet to the south. That which is to the north is the syllable Om; what is the syllable Om is the Praṇava; what is the Praṇava is all-pervading; what is all-pervading is infinite; what is infinite is the deliverer; what is the deliverer is white; what is white is subtle; what is subtle is resplendent like lightning; what is resplendent like lightning is the Supreme Brahman; what is the Supreme Brahman is the one; what is the one is Rudra; what is Rudra is Īśāna; what is Īśāna is the Blessed One, Maheśvara.

s: atha kasmād ucyate oṃkāraḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva prāṇān ūrdhvam utkrāmayati tasmād ucyate oṃkāraḥ | atha kasmād ucyate praṇavaḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvāṅgirasaṃ brahma brāhmaṇebhyaḥ praṇāmayati nāmayati ca tasmād ucyate praṇavaḥ | atha kasmād ucyate sarvavyāpī yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva yathā snehena palalapiṇḍam iva śāntarūpam otaprotam anuprāpto vyatiṣaktaś ca tasmād ucyate sarvavyāpī | atha kasmād ucyate 'nantaḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva tiryag ūrdhvam adhastāc cāsyānto nopalabhyate tasmād ucyate 'nantaḥ | atha kasmād ucyate tāraṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva garbhajanmavyādhijarāmaraṇasaṃsāramahābhayāt tārayati trāyate ca tasmād ucyate tāram | atha kasmād ucyate śuklaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva klandate klāmayati ca tasmād ucyate śuklam | atha kasmād ucyate sūkṣmaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva sūkṣmo bhūtvā śarīrāṇy adhitiṣṭhati sarvāṇi cāṅgāny abhimṛśati tasmād ucyate sūkṣmam | atha kasmād ucyate vaidyutaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva vyakte mahati tamasi dyotayati tasmād ucyate vaidyutam | atha kasmād ucyate paraṃ brahma yasmāt param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ca bṛhad bṛhatyā bṛṃhayati tasmād ucyate paraṃ brahma | atha kasmād ucyate ekaḥ yaḥ sarvān prāṇān saṃbhakṣya saṃbhakṣaṇenājaḥ saṃsṛjati visṛjati tīrtham eke vrajanti tīrtham eke dakṣiṇāḥ pratyañca udañcaḥ prāñco 'bhivrajanty eke teṣāṃ sarveṣām iha saṃgatiḥ | sākaṃ sa eko bhūtaś carati prajānāṃ tasmād ucyate ekaḥ | atha kasmād ucyate rudraḥ yasmād ṛṣibhir nānyair bhaktair drutam asya rūpam upalabhyate tasmād ucyate rudraḥ | atha kasmād ucyate īśānaḥ yaḥ sarvān devān īśate īśānībhir jananībhiś ca śaktibhiḥ | abhittvā śūraṇo numo dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ | īśānam asya jagataḥ svadarśam īśānam indratasthuṣa iti tasmād ucyate īśānaḥ | atha kasmād ucyate bhagavān maheśvaraḥ yasmād bhaktājñānena bhajaty anugṛhṇāti ca vācaṃ saṃsṛjati visṛjati ca sarvān bhāvān parityajyātmajñānena yogaiśvaryeṇa mahati mahīyate tasmād ucyate bhagavān maheśvaraḥ tad etad rudracaritam ||
d: अथ कस्माद् उच्यते ओंकारः यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव प्राणान् ऊर्ध्वम् उत्क्रामयति तस्माद् उच्यते ओंकारः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते प्रणवः यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वाङ्गिरसं ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रणामयति नामयति च तस्माद् उच्यते प्रणवः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते सर्वव्यापी यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव यथा स्नेहेन पललपिण्डम् इव शान्तरूपम् ओतप्रोतम् अनुप्राप्तो व्यतिषक्तश् च तस्माद् उच्यते सर्वव्यापी । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते ऽनन्तः यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव तिर्यग् ऊर्ध्वम् अधस्ताच् चास्यान्तो नोपलभ्यते तस्माद् उच्यते ऽनन्तः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते तारं यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव गर्भजन्मव्याधिजरामरणसंसारमहाभयात् तारयति त्रायते च तस्माद् उच्यते तारम् । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते शुक्लं यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव क्लन्दते क्लामयति च तस्माद् उच्यते शुक्लम् । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते सूक्ष्मं यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव सूक्ष्मो भूत्वा शरीराण्य् अधितिष्ठति सर्वाणि चाङ्गान्य् अभिमृशति तस्माद् उच्यते सूक्ष्मम् । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते वैद्युतं यस्माद् उच्चार्यमाण एव व्यक्ते महति तमसि द्योतयति तस्माद् उच्यते वैद्युतम् । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते परं ब्रह्म यस्मात् परम् अपरं परायणं च बृहद् बृहत्या बृंहयति तस्माद् उच्यते परं ब्रह्म । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते एकः यः सर्वान् प्राणान् संभक्ष्य संभक्षणेनाजः संसृजति विसृजति तीर्थम् एके व्रजन्ति तीर्थम् एके दक्षिणाः प्रत्यञ्च उदञ्चः प्राञ्चो ऽभिव्रजन्त्य् एके तेषां सर्वेषाम् इह संगतिः । साकं स एको भूतश् चरति प्रजानां तस्माद् उच्यते एकः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते रुद्रः यस्माद् ऋषिभिर् नान्यैर् भक्तैर् द्रुतम् अस्य रूपम् उपलभ्यते तस्माद् उच्यते रुद्रः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते ईशानः यः सर्वान् देवान् ईशते ईशानीभिर् जननीभिश् च शक्तिभिः । अभित्त्वा शूरणो नुमो दुग्धा इव धेनवः । ईशानम् अस्य जगतः स्वदर्शम् ईशानम् इन्द्रतस्थुष इति तस्माद् उच्यते ईशानः । अथ कस्माद् उच्यते भगवान् महेश्वरः यस्माद् भक्ताज्ञानेन भजत्य् अनुगृह्णाति च वाचं संसृजति विसृजति च सर्वान् भावान् परित्यज्यात्मज्ञानेन योगैश्वर्येण महति महीयते तस्माद् उच्यते भगवान् महेश्वरः तद् एतद् रुद्रचरितम् ॥
m:
Now, why is it called the syllable Om? Because as soon as it is uttered, it causes the vital breaths to rise upward, therefore it is called the syllable Om.
Now, why is it called the Praṇava? Because as soon as it is uttered, it causes the Brahman in the form of Ṛg-, Yajur-, Sāma-, and Atharvāṅgiras [Vedas] to bow and bend before the Brahmins, therefore it is called the Praṇava.
Now, why is it called all-pervading? Because as soon as it is uttered, just as oil [pervades] a lump of meat, of peaceful form, woven warp and woof, having reached and interpenetrated [all], therefore it is called all-pervading.
Now, why is it called infinite? Because as soon as it is uttered, its end is not found horizontally, upward, or downward, therefore it is called infinite.
Now, why is it called the deliverer? Because as soon as it is uttered, it delivers and saves from the great fear of the cycle of rebirth [consisting of] the womb, birth, disease, old age, and death, therefore it is called the deliverer.
Now, why is it called white? Because as soon as it is uttered, it illuminates and cleanses, therefore it is called white.
Now, why is it called subtle? Because as soon as it is uttered, having become subtle it abides in bodies and touches all limbs, therefore it is called subtle.
Now, why is it called resplendent like lightning? Because as soon as it is uttered, it shines forth in the manifest, great darkness, therefore it is called resplendent like lightning.
Now, why is it called the Supreme Brahman? Because [it is] higher than the highest, the ultimate goal, and vast, it nourishes by means of the vast, therefore it is called the Supreme Brahman.
Now, why is it called the one? Because, having consumed all vital breaths by consuming [them], unborn, he creates and emits. Some go to the holy ford, some go to the south, to the west, to the north, some proceed to the east; of all of them, the meeting is here.
Together he moves, having become the one of all beings; therefore he is called the one.
Now, why is it called Rudra? Because his form is swiftly perceived by ṛṣis, and not by others, [even] devotees; therefore he is called Rudra.
Now, why is it called Īśāna? Because he rules all gods with his ruling and generating powers.
'Breaking not, we praise the hero like milked cows,
the ruler of this moving world, pleasant to behold, the ruler, Indra, of what stands still'—therefore he is called Īśāna.
Now, why is it called the Blessed One Maheśvara? Because he favors the devotee with knowledge and shows grace; he creates speech and emits [it]; and abandoning all states, through self-knowledge and yogic power he is magnified in the great; therefore he is called the Blessed One Maheśvara. That is the course of Rudra.

s: eko ha devaḥ pradiśo 'nu sarvāḥ pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbha antaḥ | sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅjanās tiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ | eko rudro na dvitīyāya tasmai ya imāṃl lokān īśata īśānībhiḥ | pratyaṅjanās tiṣṭhati saṃcukocāntakāle saṃsṛjya viśvā bhuvanāni goptā | yo yoniṃ yonim adhitiṣṭhaty eko yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vicarati sarvam | tam īśānaṃ varadaṃ devam īḍyaṃ nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti | kṣamāṃ hitvā hetujālasya mūlaṃ buddhyā saṃcitaṃ sthāpayitvā tu rudro rudram ekatvam āhuḥ | śāśvataṃ vai purāṇam iṣam ūrjeṇa paśavo 'nunāmayantaṃ mṛtyupāśān | tad etenātmann etenārdhacaturthena mātreṇa śāntiṃ saṃsṛjati paśupāśavimokṣaṇam yā sā prathamā mātrā brahmadevatyā raktā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched brahmapadam | yā sā dvitīyā mātrā viṣṇudevatyā kṛṣṇā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched vaiṣṇavaṃ padam | yā sā tṛtīyā mātrā īśānadevatyā kapilā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched aiśānaṃ padam | yā sārdhacaturthī mātrā sarvadevatyāvyaktībhūtā khaṃ vicarati śuddhā sphaṭikasaṃnibhā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacchet padam anāmayam | tad etad upāsīta munayo vāgvadanti na tasya grahaṇam ayaṃ panthā vihita uttareṇa yena devā yānti yena pitaro yena ṛṣayaḥ param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ceti ||
d: एको ह देवः प्रदिशो ऽनु सर्वाः पूर्वो ह जातः स उ गर्भ अन्तः । स एव जातः स जनिष्यमाणः प्रत्यङ्जनास् तिष्ठति सर्वतोमुखः । एको रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्मै य इमांल् लोकान् ईशत ईशानीभिः । प्रत्यङ्जनास् तिष्ठति संचुकोचान्तकाले संसृज्य विश्वा भुवनानि गोप्ता । यो योनिं योनिम् अधितिष्ठत्य् एको येनेदं सर्वं विचरति सर्वम् । तम् ईशानं वरदं देवम् ईड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिम् अत्यन्तम् एति । क्षमां हित्वा हेतुजालस्य मूलं बुद्ध्या संचितं स्थापयित्वा तु रुद्रो रुद्रम् एकत्वम् आहुः । शाश्वतं वै पुराणम् इषम् ऊर्जेण पशवो ऽनुनामयन्तं मृत्युपाशान् । तद् एतेनात्मन्न् एतेनार्धचतुर्थेन मात्रेण शान्तिं संसृजति पशुपाशविमोक्षणम् या सा प्रथमा मात्रा ब्रह्मदेवत्या रक्ता वर्णेन यस् तां ध्यायते नित्यं स गच्छेद् ब्रह्मपदम् । या सा द्वितीया मात्रा विष्णुदेवत्या कृष्णा वर्णेन यस् तां ध्यायते नित्यं स गच्छेद् वैष्णवं पदम् । या सा तृतीया मात्रा ईशानदेवत्या कपिला वर्णेन यस् तां ध्यायते नित्यं स गच्छेद् ऐशानं पदम् । या सार्धचतुर्थी मात्रा सर्वदेवत्याव्यक्तीभूता खं विचरति शुद्धा स्फटिकसंनिभा वर्णेन यस् तां ध्यायते नित्यं स गच्छेत् पदम् अनामयम् । तद् एतद् उपासीत मुनयो वाग्वदन्ति न तस्य ग्रहणम् अयं पन्था विहित उत्तरेण येन देवा यान्ति येन पितरो येन ऋषयः परम् अपरं परायणं चेति ॥
m:
The one God indeed faces all intermediate directions; he was born first, and he is inside the womb. / He alone was born, and he is to be born; facing inward toward creatures, he stands facing every direction.
Rudra is one; they do not stand for a second to him, who rules these worlds with his ruling powers. / Facing inward toward creatures, he stands; having created all worlds, their protector, he withdraws them at the time of the end.
He who, one, presides over every womb, by whom this whole [universe] wanders, the all— / perceiving that Īśāna, the boongiver, the god worthy of praise, one attains this ultimate peace.
Abandoning tolerance [and intolerance], the root of the web of causation, having fixed [in Rudra] what has been gathered by the intellect, they declare Rudra to be oneness. / Rudra indeed, eternal and ancient, [destroys] the snares of death, causing creatures to bend food by strength.
Therefore, by this self, by this three-and-a-half mora, he generates peace, the liberation from the beasts' snare. The first mora is sacred to Brahmā, red in color; whoever meditates on it constantly, he would go to the realm of Brahmā.
The second mora is sacred to Viṣṇu, black in color; whoever meditates on it constantly, he would go to the realm of Viṣṇu.
The third mora is sacred to Īśāna, tawny in color; whoever meditates on it constantly, he would go to the realm of Īśāna.
The three-and-a-half mora is sacred to all gods; having become unmanifest, it moves through space, pure, resembling crystal in color; whoever meditates on it constantly, he would go to the disease-free realm.
One should venerate this; the sages declare the word, [yet] there is no grasping of him. This path is ordained along the north, along which the gods go, along which the ancestors go, along which the ṛṣis go, the highest, the lower, and the ultimate goal.

s: bālāgramātraṃ hṛdayasya madhye viśvaṃ devaṃ jātarūpaṃ vareṇyam | tam ātmasthaṃ ye tu paśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntir bhavati netareṣām ||
d: बालाग्रमात्रं हृदयस्य मध्ये विश्वं देवं जातरूपं वरेण्यम् । तम् आत्मस्थं ये तु पश्यन्ति धीरास् तेषां शान्तिर् भवति नेतरेषाम् ॥
m: The size of the tip of a hair, in the middle of the heart, the universal god, golden, most excellent— / the wise who see him abiding in the self, theirs is peace, not others'.

s: yasmin krodhaṃ yāṃ ca tṛṣṇāṃ kṣamāṃ cākṣamāṃ hitvā hetujālasya mūlam | buddhyā saṃcitaṃ sthāpayitvā tu rudre rudram ekatvam āhuḥ ||
d: यस्मिन् क्रोधं यां च तृष्णां क्षमां चाक्षमां हित्वा हेतुजालस्य मूलम् । बुद्ध्या संचितं स्थापयित्वा तु रुद्रे रुद्रम् एकत्वम् आहुः ॥
m: In whom [they cast off] anger, and thirst, and tolerance, and intolerance, abandoning the root of the web of causation, / having fixed in Rudra what has been gathered by the intellect, they declare Rudra to be oneness.

s: rudro hi śāśvatena vai purāṇeneṣam ūrjeṇa tapasā niyantāgnir iti bhasma vāyar iti bhasma jalam iti bhasma sthalam iti bhasma vyomam iti bhasma sarvaṃ ha vā idaṃ bhasma mana etāni cakṣūṃṣi yasmād vratam idaṃ pāśupataṃ yad bhasmanāṅgāni saṃspṛśet tasmād brahma tad etat pāśupataṃ paśupāśavimokṣaṇāya ||
d: रुद्रो हि शाश्वतेन वै पुराणेनेषम् ऊर्जेण तपसा नियन्ताग्निर् इति भस्म वायर् इति भस्म जलम् इति भस्म स्थलम् इति भस्म व्योमम् इति भस्म सर्वं ह वा इदं भस्म मन एतानि चक्षूंषि यस्माद् व्रतम् इदं पाशुपतं यद् भस्मनाङ्गानि संस्पृशेत् तस्माद् ब्रह्म तद् एतत् पाशुपतं पशुपाशविमोक्षणाय ॥
m: For Rudra is the restrainer through eternal, ancient food, through vigor and ascetic heat. 'Fire is ash, wind is ash, water is ash, earth is ash, space is ash, all this indeed is ash, the mind and these eyes.' Because this is the Pāśupata vow, that one should touch one's limbs with ash, therefore this is that Pāśupata Brahman for the release from the beast's snare.

s: yo 'gnau rudro yo 'psv antar ya oṣadhīr vīrudha āviveśa | ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni caklape tasmai rudrāya namo 'stv agnaye | yo rudro 'gnau yo rudro 'psv antar yo rudra oṣadhīr vīrudha āviveśa | yo rudra imā viśvā bhuvanāni caklape tasmai rudrāya namonamaḥ | yo rudro 'psu yo rudra oṣadhiṣu yo rudro vanaspatiṣu | yena rudreṇa jagad ūrdhvaṃ dhāritaṃ pṛthivī dvidhā tridhā dhartā dhāritā nāgā ye 'ntarikṣe tasmai rudrāya vai namonamaḥ | mūrdhānam asya saṃsevyāpy atharvā hṛdayaṃ ca yat | mastiṣkād ūrdhvaṃ prerayaty avamāno 'dhiśīrṣataḥ ||
d: यो ऽग्नौ रुद्रो यो ऽप्स्व् अन्तर् य ओषधीर् वीरुध आविवेश । य इमा विश्वा भुवनानि चक्लपे तस्मै रुद्राय नमो ऽस्त्व् अग्नये । यो रुद्रो ऽग्नौ यो रुद्रो ऽप्स्व् अन्तर् यो रुद्र ओषधीर् वीरुध आविवेश । यो रुद्र इमा विश्वा भुवनानि चक्लपे तस्मै रुद्राय नमोनमः । यो रुद्रो ऽप्सु यो रुद्र ओषधिषु यो रुद्रो वनस्पतिषु । येन रुद्रेण जगद् ऊर्ध्वं धारितं पृथिवी द्विधा त्रिधा धर्ता धारिता नागा ये ऽन्तरिक्षे तस्मै रुद्राय वै नमोनमः । मूर्धानम् अस्य संसेव्याप्य् अथर्वा हृदयं च यत् । मस्तिष्काद् ऊर्ध्वं प्रेरयत्य् अवमानो ऽधिशीर्षतः ॥
m: The Rudra who is in fire, who is within water, who has entered herbs and plants, / who fashioned all these worlds—to that Rudra, to Agni, be homage! / The Rudra who is in fire, the Rudra who is within water, the Rudra who has entered herbs and plants, / the Rudra who fashioned all these worlds—to that Rudra, homage, homage! / The Rudra who is in waters, the Rudra who is in herbs, the Rudra who is in trees, / by which Rudra the world is held aloft, the earth twofold, threefold, the bearer, held, and the serpents that are in the intermediate space—to that Rudra indeed be homage, homage! / Having also honored his head and that which is the heart of Atharvan, / the cleansing [breath] impels upward from the brain over the head.

s: tad vā atharvaṇaḥ śiro devakośaḥ samujjhitaḥ | tat prāṇo 'bhirakṣati śiro 'ntam atho manaḥ | na ca divo devajanena guptā na cāntarikṣāṇi na ca bhūma imāḥ yasminn idaṃ sarvam otaprotaṃ tasmād anyaṃ na paraṃ kiṃca nāsti ||
d: तद् वा अथर्वणः शिरो देवकोशः समुज्झितः । तत् प्राणो ऽभिरक्षति शिरो ऽन्तम् अथो मनः । न च दिवो देवजनेन गुप्ता न चान्तरिक्षाणि न च भूम इमाः यस्मिन्न् इदं सर्वम् ओतप्रोतं तस्माद् अन्यं न परं किंच नास्ति ॥
m: That indeed is the head of Atharvan, the vessel of the gods, cast forth; / that head, the end, and then the mind, the vital breath protects. / Neither the heavens are protected by the race of gods, nor the intermediate spaces, nor these earths; [he] in whom all this is woven warp and woof—other than him, there is nothing higher whatsoever.

s: na tasmāt pūrvaṃ na paraṃ tad asti na bhūtaṃ nota bhavyaṃ yad āsīt | sahasrapād ekamūrdhnā vyāptaṃ sa evedam āvarīvartti bhūtam ||
d: न तस्मात् पूर्वं न परं तद् अस्ति न भूतं नोत भव्यं यद् आसीत् । सहस्रपाद् एकमूर्ध्ना व्याप्तं स एवेदम् आवरीवर्त्ति भूतम् ॥
m: There is nothing prior to him, nor is there anything beyond him; there is neither past nor future that existed [apart from him]. / Having a thousand feet, pervading all with a single head, he alone keeps turning this world of beings around and around.

s: akṣarāt saṃjāyate kālaḥ kālād vyāpaka ucyate ||
d: अक्षरात् संजायते कालः कालाद् व्यापक उच्यते ॥
m: From the imperishable, time is born; from time, the all-pervading is proclaimed.

s: vyāpako hi bhagavān rudro bhogāyamāno yadā śete rudras tadā saṃhāryyate prajāḥ | ucchvasite tamo bhavati tamasa āpo 'psv aṅgulyā mathite mathitaṃ śiśire śiśiraṃ mathyamānaṃ phenaṃ bhavati phenād aṇḍaṃ bhavaty aṇḍād brahmā bhavati brahmaṇo vāyuḥ vāyor oṃkāraḥ oṃkārāt sāvitrī sāvitryā gāyatrī gāyatryā lokā bhavanti | arcayanti tapaḥ satyaṃ madhu kṣaranti yad dhruvam | etaddhi paramaṃ tapaḥ | āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtaṃ brahma bhūr bhuvaḥ svar oṃ nama iti ||
d: व्यापको हि भगवान् रुद्रो भोगायमानो यदा शेते रुद्रस् तदा संहार्य्यते प्रजाः । उच्छ्वसिते तमो भवति तमस आपो ऽप्स्व् अङ्गुल्या मथिते मथितं शिशिरे शिशिरं मथ्यमानं फेनं भवति फेनाद् अण्डं भवत्य् अण्डाद् ब्रह्मा भवति ब्रह्मणो वायुः वायोर् ओंकारः ओंकारात् सावित्री सावित्र्या गायत्री गायत्र्या लोका भवन्ति । अर्चयन्ति तपः सत्यं मधु क्षरन्ति यद् ध्रुवम् । एतद्धि परमं तपः । आपो ज्योती रसो ऽमृतं ब्रह्म भूर् भुवः स्वर् ओं नम इति ॥
m: For the Blessed One Rudra is the all-pervading. When Rudra lies down, taking his rest, then creatures are withdrawn. / When he breathes out, darkness arises; from darkness, the waters. When churned in the waters with a finger, that which is churned turns into cold; the cold, being churned, becomes foam; from the foam an egg arises; from the egg Brahmā arises; from Brahmā, Vāyu; from Vāyu, the syllable Om; from the syllable Om, the Sāvitrī meter; from the Sāvitrī meter, the Gāyatrī; from the Gāyatrī, the worlds arise. / They worship ascetic heat and truth, which stream forth constant honey. / For this indeed is the supreme ascetic heat: / 'Water, light, essence, nectar of immortality, Brahman, Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Om, homage.'

s: ya idam atharvaśiro brāhmaṇo 'dhīte aśrotriyaḥ śrotriyo bhavati anupanīta upanīto bhavati so 'gnipūto bhavati sa vāyupūto bhavati sa sūryapūto bhavati sa somapūto bhavati sa satyapūto bhavati sa sarvair devair jñāto bhavati sa sarvair vedair anudhyāto bhavati sa sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snāto bhavati tena sarvaiḥ kratubhir iṣṭaṃ bhavati gāyatryāḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi japtāni bhavanti itihāsapurāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ śatasahasrāṇi japtāni bhavanti | praṇavānām ayutaṃ japtaṃ bhavati | sa cakṣuṣaḥ paṅktiṃ punāti | ā saptamāt puruṣayugān punātīty āha bhagavān atharvaśiraḥ sakṛj japtvaiva śuciḥ sa pūtaḥ karmaṇyo bhavati | dvitīyaṃ japtvā gaṇādhipatyam āpnoti | tṛtīyaṃ japtvaivam evānupraviśaty oṃ satyam oṃ satyam oṃ satyam ||
d: य इदम् अथर्वशिरो ब्राह्मणो ऽधीते अश्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियो भवति अनुपनीत उपनीतो भवति सो ऽग्निपूतो भवति स वायुपूतो भवति स सूर्यपूतो भवति स सोमपूतो भवति स सत्यपूतो भवति स सर्वैर् देवैर् ज्ञातो भवति स सर्वैर् वेदैर् अनुध्यातो भवति स सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु स्नातो भवति तेन सर्वैः क्रतुभिर् इष्टं भवति गायत्र्याः षष्टिसहस्राणि जप्तानि भवन्ति इतिहासपुराणानां रुद्राणां शतसहस्राणि जप्तानि भवन्ति । प्रणवानाम् अयुतं जप्तं भवति । स चक्षुषः पङ्क्तिं पुनाति । आ सप्तमात् पुरुषयुगान् पुनातीत्य् आह भगवान् अथर्वशिरः सकृज् जप्त्वैव शुचिः स पूतः कर्मण्यो भवति । द्वितीयं जप्त्वा गणाधिपत्यम् आप्नोति । तृतीयं जप्त्वैवम् एवानुप्रविशत्य् ओं सत्यम् ओं सत्यम् ओं सत्यम् ॥
m: The Brahmin who recites this Atharvaśiras: if he is not a Vedic scholar, he becomes a Vedic scholar; if uninitiated, he becomes initiated. He becomes purified by Agni, he becomes purified by Vāyu, he becomes purified by Sūrya, he becomes purified by Soma, he becomes purified by truth. He becomes recognized by all the gods, he becomes meditated upon by all the Vedas, he becomes bathed in all the sacred fords, by him sacrifices have been offered with all rites. Sixty thousand [repetitions] of the Gāyatrī have been recited, a hundred thousand [repetitions] of the Itihāsas, Purāṇas, and Rudras have been recited, / ten thousand Praṇavas have been recited. / He purifies the row of diners as far as his eye can see; / he purifies up to seven generations of men—so says the Blessed One. By reciting the Atharvaśiras just once, he becomes pure, purified, and fit for rituals. / By reciting it a second time, he attains sovereignty over the Gaṇas. / By reciting it a third time, he enters into [the divine] itself: Om truth, Om truth, Om truth. / Thus ends the Śiras Upaniṣad in the Atharvaveda.
